title: $400K AI Job Nobody's Heard Of
description:
There's a tech job right now where mid-level engineers reportedly make $300–400K, job postings grew over 1,000% in a single year, and most developers have never heard of it. It's called a forward-deployed engineer, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Palantir are all fighting over the same small pool of people who can do it. 

The interesting part: it's not a high-level PhD research role. The skills are mostly things a solid developer can pick up fairly quickly, but stacked in one specific combination that almost nobody has.

#techwithtim #aiengineer #techjobs

top_reply.author: @7schoGamer
top_reply.text:
In theory all jobs can be taken over, however developing a specific AI costs money. For example, right now there are 100 engineers in your area and their salary is like $50 per year, then it’s profitable for an AI company to spend under $5000 to develop an AI. The current situation is the hardware is not advanced and not cheap enough for them to develop those AI with lower cost. So a job looks secure now may get replaced 10 years later. 

Another thing is you can let one AI to teach you how to use another AI. 
Let’s say you are running a company and don’t know anything about coding, then 10 years ago you need to hire someone to code for you. 
But 2 years ago, you still need to hire someone to code for you, not knowing that guy is actually using a “coding AI” to help him code faster. 
But now or very soon, you don’t need to hire someone else to code for you, you can just ask one AI about how to use the “coding AI” to code yourself. 
Or even in the future, you just tell the AI what you want, and it will talk to the “coding AI” to get what you wanted (without your involvement).
